###Data management using dpylr package

##Exploring mtcars dataset
```{r}
library(dplyr)
data(mtcars)
head(mtcars)
tail(mtcars)
str(mtcars)
summary(mtcars)
```

#Select: choosing columns
```{r}
cars <- mtcars %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("car")
cars %>% select(car, mpg, cyl, hp)
cars %>% select(-qsec, -vs)             # drop columns
cars %>% select(car, starts_with("d"))  # by name pattern
cars %>% select(where(is.numeric))      # by type
```


#Filter: keeping rows that meet with conditions
```{r}
cars %>% filter(mpg > 25)
cars %>% filter(cyl == 4, hp > 80)          # AND
cars %>% filter(cyl == 4 | cyl == 6)        # OR
cars %>% filter(cyl %in% c(4, 6))
cars %>% filter(between(mpg, 20, 30))
```

#Arrange: sorting rows
```{r}
cars %>% arrange(mpg)            # ascending
cars %>% arrange(desc(hp))       # descending
cars %>% arrange(cyl, desc(mpg)) # by several columns
```

#Mutate: creating or modifying columns
```{r}
cars <- cars %>%
  mutate(
    wt_kg     = wt * 453.6,                      # wt is in 1000 lbs
    kpl       = mpg * 0.425,                     # km per litre
    hp_per_wt = hp / wt,
    cyl       = factor(cyl),
    am        = factor(am, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Automatic", "Manual")),
    efficiency = case_when(
      mpg >= 25 ~ "High",
      mpg >= 18 ~ "Medium",
      TRUE      ~ "Low"
    ))
```

#Rename: changing columns name
```{r}
cars <- cars %>% rename(miles_per_gallon = mpg, horsepower = hp)
```

#Group_by()+ summarize(): summarising by group
```{r}
cars %>%
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    mean_mpg = mean(miles_per_gallon),
    sd_mpg   = sd(miles_per_gallon),
    max_hp   = max(horsepower)
  )

# Two grouping variables
cars %>%
  group_by(cyl, am) %>%
  summarise(mean_mpg = mean(miles_per_gallon), .groups = "drop")

# Summarise many columns at once
cars %>%
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  summarise(across(c(miles_per_gallon, horsepower, wt), mean))
```

#Counting and ranking
```{r}
cars %>% count(cyl)
cars %>% count(cyl, am, sort = TRUE)

cars %>% slice_max(miles_per_gallon, n = 5)   # top 5 by mpg
cars %>% slice_min(horsepower, n = 3)         # lowest 3 by hp
cars %>% slice_sample(n = 5)                  # random 5 rows

cars %>% mutate(rank = min_rank(desc(miles_per_gallon)))
```

#Data cleaning
```{r}
cars %>% distinct(cyl, gear)                # unique combinations
sum(duplicated(cars))                       # duplicate rows
cars %>% filter(!is.na(miles_per_gallon))   # remove missing values
colSums(is.na(cars))                        # missing values per column
```


#Joining data: Creating a small lookup table and merge it

```{r}
origin <- data.frame(
  cyl    = factor(c(4, 6, 8)),
  engine = c("Small", "Medium", "Large")
)

cars %>%
  left_join(origin, by = "cyl") %>%
  select(car, cyl, engine)
```
